analysis.title: Europe Open - Week of reckoning
key_insights: Modest moves across markets at the start of a catalyst-heavy week. USTs lifted on lower volumes, FX rangebound, stocks mixed. US equity futures rose tentatively on news Iran will host security and defense officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, but conviction stalled into the London session.

Moody's affirmed France's sovereign rating at Aa3 with a negative outlook on Friday. Citi expects OAT spreads to tighten modestly at the open but sees any relief as temporary, since S&P and Fitch have already downgraded France and a budget vote is due Oct. 27. 10y OAT-Bund peaked at 176bp last week.

Brazil's runoff was won by President Lula with 51.8% vs Flavio Bolsonaro's 48.2%. Bolsonaro contests the result and accuses the Supreme Court of changing the rules by extending voting two hours. Citi expects a sharp selloff in Brazilian assets at the open given long positioning, with possible broader EM risk reduction.

Rates desk: activity muted at 0.6x of recent averages (down from 0.9x), with better bidding in US 10s, which traded at 4.96%. Rates strategists are receiving Oct OIS (+2.2bp priced, assuming a Dec hike), consider a Dec/Jan OIS flattener, expect the 5y to outperform on safe-haven rallies, and recommend a costless 3m forward 2s5s bull flattener.

Equities: last week's moves look like position de-grossing and/or rotation. Citi's equity desk does not like the risk/reward of fading these drivers yet, because earnings face a very high bar and large embedded P&L remains in key positions. About 41% of SPX market cap reports this week.

FX: USD rallied modestly after bottoming, with key levels holding (1.12 in EURUSD, 157 in USDJPY). G10 gamma is well supported into FOMC/ECB/BoJ/RBNZ/AU CPI. USDMXN and USDZAR volumes were 4x and 2x recent averages, likely on the Brazil result.

Commodities: possible Middle East mediation pushed oil lower, with Brent meeting resistance at $114. Trump said it is 'getting to be decision time' on a deal with Tehran or resuming attacks. Citi says risk of US/Israel escalation remains high. The State Department is drawing down personnel at several Gulf embassies.

Week ahead: the October FOMC is widely expected to hold, with Warsh's guidance key. BoJ, BoC and ECB expected to hold. RBNZ is expected to hike 25bp. AU CPI is the last data point before an expected Nov RBA hike. UK Autumn Budget on Wednesday may show £15bn of fiscal headroom. $213bn of US supply is scheduled.

Weekly Macro Brief (Jim McCormick): with DM real yields near multi-year highs, surging energy prices, French spreads at crisis levels and cracks around the AI boom, implied vol looks too low. He recommends buying protection, and sees yen vol as a way to position for a sharp USDJPY move lower. In an AI sell-off he expects UST curve steepening, not bull flattening.

RBA's Hunter said the inflation fight is 'not quite yet done', lifting AU bond yields. Germany's Ifo is expected unchanged at 89.8 (Citi est.), and Citi says its predictive value has weakened. SBP is seen not needing to hike again after a 50bp April hike, though consensus expects 50bp.
earnings_insights: About 41% of SPX market cap reports earnings this week. Citi's equity desk says earnings face a very high bar and that disappointment could drive another leg of de-risking. AI financing remains a top concern.

US/Israel escalation with Iran, and threats to American diplomats.
Position de-grossing and a high bar for earnings this week.
AI financing concerns and cracks surfacing around the AI boom.
Contested Brazil election and EM risk reduction.
DM real yields near multi-year highs and surging energy prices.
charts_described: Chart of the Day: 10yr EMU-Bund spread regressed against Bund, Bund ASW, EA FCI, equities, vol and rating-matched credit using daily data since 2020. Citi says the OAT risk premium is in uncharted territory and spreading to other EGB spreads.
vol_and_positioning: G10 gamma remains well supported into FOMC/ECB/BoJ/RBNZ/AU CPI, with implied moves priced at 47.5bps, 20bps and 50bps for the first three.
Jim McCormick says implied vol in most markets looks too low relative to the risks and recommends buying protection. Yen vol is a good way to position for a potential explosive USDJPY move lower.
Equity desk sees last week's moves as de-grossing and/or rotation with large embedded P&L still in key positions, leaving room for another leg of de-risking.
Long positioning in Brazilian assets into the election is cited as a reason for a sharp selloff.
Spot interbank FX volumes were in line with 30-day averages in Asia, while flows remain extremely muted.
geopolitical: Iran will host top security and defense officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey for regional security talks, per Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Ali Bagheri Kani.
Saudi deputy minister for public diplomacy is expected to meet Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian and SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaee.
Trump said the Iran conflict will end soon 'one way or another' and that it is 'getting to be decision time' on a deal or resumed attacks.
Axios reports US intel found Iran has 'substantially increased' efforts to target American diplomats, and the State Department is drawing down personnel at several Gulf embassies.
Brazil's runoff result is contested by Bolsonaro, who has called for annulment and accused the Supreme Court of changing the rules.
Israel general elections are on Tuesday, and the US midterms are one week away.

tension_points.bull_case: Moody's affirmed Aa3, French Finance Minister Lescure said it reflects underlying economic strength, and OAT spreads may tighten modestly at the open.
tension_points.bear_case: S&P and Fitch have already downgraded, the outlook is negative, a budget vote is due Oct. 27 and the fiscal trajectory is not improving, so Citi sees limited scope for a sustained reversal.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material improvement in the fiscal trajectory, such as passage of the Oct. 27 budget vote, would challenge the bear case.
